item.title: Managing Retail Promotional Peaks: Capacity, Cross-Docking, and Returns
item.description:
What are the Key Takeaways from this Executive Summary?

Quick answer

A promotional peak tests three things: whether you can get trucks, whether stock can cross the warehouse without being put away, and whether you can handle the returns that follow. Each one can be prepared before the peak. None can be fixed during it.
  • Cross-docking keeps fast stock moving. Instead of putting a pallet away and picking it again later, you move it straight from the inbound door to the outbound trailer.
  • Get spare carrier capacity agreed in advance. When your main carriers turn down loads, you need a second and third option already priced, not a phone call on the day.
  • Plan the returns before the peak, not after it. Returns arrive a few weeks behind the sales. If nobody has planned for them, they block the dock you need for outbound.
